labels.adjacent: The technique or barrier is known, but in a different setting, or the literature only implies it.
labels.not-found: No retrieved abstract states the barrier after a reasonable search.
labels.published: A retrieved abstract states the same barrier for the same problem setting; the records add at most instances.
labels.unclear: The cluster is too heterogeneous or its records too terse to judge.

CFI-STRUCTURAL-DECODER-DEQUANTIZED-PETER.label: published
CFI-STRUCTURAL-DECODER-DEQUANTIZED-PETER.note: label=published; 2107.03778 states that the CFI-query (twist parity of an unordered CFI graph) is in PTIME, which is exactly the record's barrier. The Petersen base graph is only an instance.

CODE-FRONTIER-TRIAGE-HAMMING_7_4_PERMUTE.label: published
CODE-FRONTIER-TRIAGE-HAMMING_7_4_PERMUTE.note: label=published; A permuted [7,4] Hamming code is an equivalent control that classical canonicalization and code-equivalence algorithms resolve. The fit is weak because SSA struggles with transitive automorphism groups, but n=7 is trivially classical.

CODE-STRUCTURAL-INVARIANT-REJECTED-CODE_.label: published
CODE-STRUCTURAL-INVARIANT-REJECTED-CODE_.note: label=published; Support splitting and punctured/shortened weight profiles are published classical code-equivalence invariants (1111.4382 cites Sendrier's SSA as a classical attack). This random [12,5] pair is an instance.

CODE-STRUCTURAL-INVARIANT-REJECTED-CODE_.label: published
CODE-STRUCTURAL-INVARIANT-REJECTED-CODE_.note: label=published; Hull dimension, support splitting and punctured/shortened weight profiles are published classical code-equivalence invariants (1111.4382, 1905.00073). This random [9,4] pair is an instance.

FINITE-CARRIER-BRANCH-SUCCESS-NOT-ALL-N-.label: published
FINITE-CARRIER-BRANCH-SUCCESS-NOT-ALL-N-.note: label=published; quant-ph/0504067 and quant-ph/0401083 already state that a finite-n success certificate for a hidden-involution measurement is not an efficient algorithm without an efficient circuit and decoder. Only the finite-to-all-n proof gap is project-specific.

HS-DEQUANTIZED-QUADRATIC_CHIRP.label: unclear
HS-DEQUANTIZED-QUADRATIC_CHIRP.note: label=adjacent; The record is clear: a quadratic-chirp hidden shift is recovered classically from an explicit evaluator, because the shift difference is a linear phase. This is known for Boolean quadratic/bent hidden shifts (2408.02778, folklore O(n)-query attack); a chirp is a neighbouring setting.

LEGACY-BERNSTEIN_VAZIRANI.label: adjacent
LEGACY-BERNSTEIN_VAZIRANI.note: label=adjacent; A procedural rejection: an N=3 custom-oracle simulation is not evidence of speedup. This parallels known speedup-detection pitfalls (1401.2910) in another setting. The record is terse, and BV itself is a published algorithm covered by oracle identification.

LEGACY-NONLINEARTERNARYPRODUCTSUMSECRETF.label: adjacent
LEGACY-NONLINEARTERNARYPRODUCTSUMSECRETF.note: label=adjacent; A procedural rejection (N=3 cap, zero simulation successes, no scalable family). Speedup-detection pitfalls and oracle-identification query bounds are known, but no abstract states this barrier for this problem.

LEGACY-NOVEL_NONLINEAR_BITWISE_ROTATION_.label: adjacent
LEGACY-NOVEL_NONLINEAR_BITWISE_ROTATION_.note: label=adjacent; A procedural rejection (N=3 cap, zero simulation successes, no scalable family). Speedup-detection pitfalls and oracle-identification query bounds are known, but no abstract states this barrier for this problem.

NEG-CODE-SELF-DUAL-AUTOMORPHISM-SELF-DUA.label: published
NEG-CODE-SELF-DUAL-AUTOMORPHISM-SELF-DUA.note: label=published; 1008.2390 and 1805.09972 extend the no-go to hidden subgroups given by code automorphism groups, provided they are small with large minimal degree. The record only certifies that this instance is non-rigid, which falls under that known condition.

NEG-CODE-SELF-DUAL-HIGH-ORDER-RIGID-SELF.label: published
NEG-CODE-SELF-DUAL-HIGH-ORDER-RIGID-SELF.note: label=published; The record only certifies that this instance is rigid, which puts it in the hidden-involution case where Dinh-Moore-Russell (1008.2390) show coset-state measurements fail for codes with small automorphism group. It adds an instance, not a new barrier.

NEG-CODE-SELF-DUAL-SELF-DUAL-K6-01-05.label: adjacent
NEG-CODE-SELF-DUAL-SELF-DUAL-K6-01-05.note: label=adjacent; The trivial-hull reduction to GI is published (1905.00073). The record's own point, that small random self-dual codes collide so a large hull does not guarantee hardness, is only implied by the literature, not stated.

NEG-CODE-SELF-DUAL-WREATH-SCALAR-SUBSET-.label: adjacent
NEG-CODE-SELF-DUAL-WREATH-SCALAR-SUBSET-.note: label=adjacent; The record's barrier (Hamming-weight orbit sums do not commute, so there is no (k+1)-dim commutative algebra) differs from the cluster's pair-local PGM barrier, and the cited abstracts do not state it. It is known elsewhere: S_k-invariant algebras are noncommutative (Schur-Weyl/Terwilliger).

NEG-COSET-FINITE-NATURAL-PGM-NOT-EFFICIE.label: published
NEG-COSET-FINITE-NATURAL-PGM-NOT-EFFICIE.note: label=published; quant-ph/0504067 and quant-ph/0401083 state that information-theoretically adequate multiregister measurements for the GI-type hidden-involution HSP do not give efficient algorithms. The record restates this for its finite-n PGM.

NEG-COSET-KRONECKER-COUNT-AS-TRANSFORM.label: unclear
NEG-COSET-KRONECKER-COUNT-AS-TRANSFORM.note: label=adjacent; The barrier (counting or projecting a Kronecker multiplicity space gives no basis or amplitudes) is not the cluster's polar-cost bound and is absent from the cited QLS/polar abstracts. It parallels the known weak- versus strong-Fourier-sampling gap in HSP.

NEG-COSET-STABLE-LEAKAGE-AS-SINGLE-COMPL.label: adjacent
NEG-COSET-STABLE-LEAKAGE-AS-SINGLE-COMPL.note: label=not-found; The record's barrier (leakage spreads over every character-allowed complementary sector, so one extra intermediate partition cannot close the associator) differs from the cluster's spectral-gap/circuit barrier. No cited abstract states it or clearly implies it.

NEG-COSET-TRANSPOSITION-SIGNATURE-ALONE-.label: adjacent
NEG-COSET-TRANSPOSITION-SIGNATURE-ALONE-.note: label=adjacent; Kemp-Ramgoolam 1911.11649 studies the same question (telling Young diagrams apart by central class sums), but the abstract only poses it. The paper body shows T_2 alone fails beyond n=5, so this is borderline published; the record adds stable-range collisions.

NEG-DCP-IID-EXACT-LINEAR-HASH-BIN-PARSEV.label: adjacent
NEG-DCP-IID-EXACT-LINEAR-HASH-BIN-PARSEV.note: label=adjacent; The Parseval/variance bound for linear iid bucket estimators is not stated in the DCP abstracts. It is implied, for a restricted estimator class, by the known DCP sample-versus-time tradeoffs (Ettinger-Hoyer, Kuperberg, Bacon-Childs-van Dam).

NEG-DCP-QW-HISTORY-INDEPENDENCE-AS-REGEV.note: label=not-found; Mis-clustered. The record is a DCP/quantum-walk interface gap (walk-internal history independence does not certify the outputs Regev's reduction needs), not symmetric-group Fourier sampling. The cited S_n abstracts do not address it.

NEG-WREATH-COSET-PERMUTATION-HOLEVO-INFO.note: label=published; The barrier (O(1) coset copies carry negligible information about the hidden permutation, so Omega(n log n) entangled copies are needed) is stated by Hallgren-Roetteler-Sen and Moore-Russell-Schulman for the S_n wr Z_2 / GI setting. The Holevo/Fano bound only adds a specific estimate.

REP-SFS-NOGO-S12.note: label=published; Same barrier, same setting: single-register strong Fourier sampling over S_n reveals essentially nothing about a hidden permutation (quant-ph/0501056), so collective measurements are required (quant-ph/0511149). S_12 is just an instance.

SCHUR-COMPANION-FINAL-ROOT-RAW-METRIC-AC.note: label=adjacent; Singular values of O(w^-1/2) forcing Omega(sqrt(w)) cost for QSVT or amplification is the known condition-number/normalization lower bound (HHL, 2101.11868, 2007.15698). The record applies it to a new setting, the hidden-involution polar hierarchy.

SCHUR-COMPANION-FIXED-ARITY-WELL-CONDITI.note: label=adjacent; The barrier (two well-conditioned positive generators already generate all of M_D(C), so algebra dimension is no circuit lower bound) is a standard Burnside-type fact, not the cluster's polar-cost bound. The cited QLS/polar abstracts do not state it.

SCHUR-REJECT-SCHUR_CODE_EQUIVALENCE_WORK.label: published
SCHUR-REJECT-SCHUR_CODE_EQUIVALENCE_WORK.note: label=published; 2603.23230 and 1203.6686 state that Schur (componentwise) products of punctured or shortened codes give poly-time PEP invariants and easy instances. The random [8,4] pair is a specific instance.
